issues.legal_issue: A municipality cannot assess a rate on the stated annual letting value of buildings by fixing that value solely by reference to floor area, without a basis connecting the calculation to the rent reasonably expected from letting the buildings.
material_facts: The municipality assessed rates on mills, factories, and related buildings by assigning an annual letting value according to floor area alone.
The affected property included structures of different kinds, including factory buildings, warehouses, godowns, and shops.
There was no evidence that the different structures could reasonably be let at the uniform rate used in the calculation.
Because the assessment turned on floor area rather than rental value, a taxpayer’s objection was effectively confined to the area and not the valuation.
The affected taxpayer paid the demanded taxes under protest and sued to recover the amounts claimed to exceed the taxes lawfully due.
issues.conclusion: The floor-area rule was illegal and ultra vires, and the appeals were allowed, restoring the decrees that had restrained demands based on that rule.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 73, 75, and 78 of the Bombay Municipal Boroughs Act, 1925, a rate on lands or buildings could be assessed on capital value or annual letting value. Section 3(1) defined annual letting value by reference to the rent for which the property might reasonably be expected to let from year to year. A municipality could not substitute an unsanctioned method that ignored both bases, bore no demonstrated relationship to expected rent, and made the statutory opportunity to object to valuation ineffective. The Privy Council decision in The Madras and Southern Mahratta Railway Co. Ltd. v. The Bezwada Municipality was distinguished because it concerned a different statutory scheme and a recognised method of estimating rent. The approach in The Borough Municipality of Amalner v. The Pratap Spinning, Weaving and Manufacturing Co. Ltd. was not approved. Motiram Keshavdas v. Ahmedabad Municipal Borough was referred to regarding a levy not dependent on property value.

rule.if: municipal_rate_assessment_case and annual_rental_value_is_assessment_basis and floor_area_alone_sets_value and (no_evidence_area_method_reflects_expected_rent or materially_dissimilar_buildings_are_assessed_uniformly or taxpayer_objection_is_limited_to_area)

predicates.municipal_rate_assessment_case: A proceeding concerns a municipality’s assessment or demand of a rate on land or buildings.
predicates.annual_rental_value_is_assessment_basis: The municipality assesses the rate on a value stated to represent the rent reasonably expected from letting the property.
predicates.floor_area_alone_sets_value: The municipality fixes the stated value solely by reference to the floor area of the property.
predicates.no_evidence_area_method_reflects_expecte: The municipality offers no evidence that its floor-area calculation reflects the rent reasonably expected from letting the property.
predicates.materially_dissimilar_buildings_are_asse: The municipality applies a uniform calculation to buildings that differ in kind or rental character.
predicates.taxpayer_objection_is_limited_to_area: The assessment process effectively confines the taxpayer’s objection to the property’s area rather than its rental valuation.

issues.definition: When a municipal rate assessment represents its basis as expected annual rent but uses floor area alone without a demonstrated rental basis, and the assessment also lacks rental support, treats dissimilar buildings uniformly, or limits objections to area, the floor-area-based rule is invalid.
